title: Field Ops: Inference snippets + triage playbook (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, field-friendly reference for PS/solutions engineers and sellers when diagnosing inference objections and running fast on-site / call triage. Not a final deck — more of a sticky cheat-sheet + snippets library we can paste into call notes and playbooks.

High-level goal:
- Reduce demo-to-purchase friction caused by performance/cost/security questions
- Give short, reproducible responses for common objections (latency, cost, fallback, privacy)
- Provide a 10-minute triage that surfaces the root cause and a recommended short-term mitigation

Quick TL;DR pitch snippets (30–45s):
- Latency focused: "We ship a runtime optimized for steady low P99s across common seq lengths. For most chat flows we hit X–Y ms with our curated open models; if you need tighter SLOs we can reserve Dedicated pools and tune batching/cache settings for predictable tail latency."
- Cost focused: "We lower per-token cost by automatic prefix/KV caching and batching suggestions; we’ll run a workload snapshot and give a 3-line optimization plan that usually reduces token spend 20–45% without retraining."
- Security/compliance: "Private option (VPC/on-prem) + KMS/HSM integration and audit logs for enterprise compliance — we can include an audit package and SOC/ISO artifacts under NDA."

10-minute triage flow (exact steps to run during discovery/demo):
1) Ask what they measure: token cost, p99 latency, mean latency, throughput (rps), error rate.
2) Confirm model + sequence length distribution: short prompts (<128), medium (128–512), long (>512).
3) Reproduce approximate load: single-user vs batch (show rough numbers).
4) Check obvious config: streaming enabled? response chunking? prompt length trimming?
5) Quick mitigation suggestions (pick one): move to lower-cap model variant; enable prefix cache for repeated system prompts; reduce top-p/temp for shorter responses; add chunked streaming.

Minimal data to ask for (on first call):
- Example prompt and expected response length (tokens)
- Approx concurrent users / rps expected
- Target latency SLO (p50/p95/p99)
- Monthly token volume estimate
- Any regulatory constraints (data residency, logging)

Common objections + short answers (copyable):
- "Your latency is too high": "We can set up a short perf run. Typical short-chat P95 on our hosted path is 80–150ms depending on model; Dedicated pools give tighter guarantees. If you send a sample prompt we’ll simulate and propose batching/cache settings in 48h."
- "Your price is higher than competitors": "Price varies by model and serving profile. We provide per-route cost breakdowns and an Optimize report — we’ll run a 2-week snapshot and show concrete unit-economics and a 3-step cut plan (quantization, cache, routing) to hit your target."
- "We need private on-prem": "We have a Private deployment package with VPC control plane, optional on-prem nodes, and KMS/HSM. We’ll share the checklist and typical timeline (6–10 weeks) for pilot + compliance review under NDA."

Mini benchmark table (copy into slide quickly) — example numbers for demo only:
- Model: rwl-1.2-medium | Seq: 256 | Mode: interactive | P95 latency: 120ms | Cost/token: $0.00021
- Model: rwl-1.2-small  | Seq: 128 | Mode: interactive | P95 latency: 85ms  | Cost/token: $0.00015
- Model: llama-2-q4-13b  | Seq: 512 | Mode: batch       | P95 latency: 220ms | Cost/token: $0.00045
(Disclaimer: numbers are illustrative; run a verification job for contract-level claims.)

Fallback mapping (rapid guidance for SREs/sellers):
- If P99 spikes during bursts: enable burst capacity on Dedicated OR route to a slightly smaller model variant for burst traffic.
- If cost is primary: suggest quantized variant + caching + route non-critical requests to cheaper tier.
- If hallucinations or quality regressions: pin to verified model version + run eval suite (we provide baseline prompt set) and hold canary rollout.

Sample 3-step onboarding checklist for a pilot (use in customer email):
1) Shared artifacts: sample prompts, expected outputs, traffic profile, and security requirements.
2) We run a 48–72h verification perf run and return an Optimize report with suggested config and cost forecast.
3) Kickoff pilot: one-week smoke, two-week canary at small scale, then ramp with rollback policy.

Quick canned Slack templates (paste into thread):
- To engineering contact: "Hey @eng, can you share a 1–2 minute recording of the slow flow + the exact prompt and avg token length? We're going to simulate locally to reproduce the p95 spike."
- To SRE/infra: "We’re seeing tail latency on demo environment during bursts. Can we get GPU utilization logs for the last 24h and confirm batching toggles?"

Objection handling ladder (short):
1) Acknowledge + quantify: "Totally—can you share the p95/p99 metric?"
2) Quick mitigations live on call (try smaller model, caching)
3) Commit to verification run (48–72h) and deliver measurable optimizations

Escalation contacts (for field only):
- First escalation (performance deep-dive): Marcus Lee (SE) — marcus.lee@redwood.ai
- Platform/SRE contact: Claire Huang (SRE lead) — claire.huang@redwood.ai
- Security/compliance: Aisha Patel (Security) — aisha.patel@redwood.ai

Open questions / To resolve in next iteration:
- Do we want a short canonical set of 6 benchmark prompts for Sales to always use? (pro: consistent, con: might not match buyer workload)
- Standardize a single pilot timeline for field proposals (6 vs 8 weeks?)
- Confirm one canonical ‘cheapest-but-supported’ model variant name we can use in price comparisons.

Notes to self (rough):
- Populate Confluence page with reproducible perf job steps (docker command, sample payloads).
- Create a one-pager sell sheet for Dedicated burst guarantees.
- Short video clip demoing how to flip caches/batching in Console (45s).

Next steps (owners):
- Diego: draft 6 canonical prompts and add to Confluence (due 2026-03-20)
- Marcus: prepare quick perf job template and run against two customer samples (due 2026-03-18)
- Aisha: collate SOC/ISO artifacts for private deployment one-pager (due 2026-03-25)

History / context:
- Born from repeated field asks in Q4 2025: too many ad-hoc perf objections slowing deals. This is intended to be friction-reducing, not a full engineering runbook.

If using in a slide or battlecard: keep it short — 3 bullets max per objection, include clear ask for customer artifacts, and promise a concrete deliverable (Optimize report or perf run) on the next touch.

END OF NOTE: paste/adapt as needed.
